web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: What the Market Price Assumes — Valuation, Comps & Reverse DCF
question: At ₹1,807.20 per share, what profit and cash-flow growth is the market pricing in, and how does Aurobindo compare with its history and Indian peers?

epigraph.quote: Every stock quote is an implicit multi-year cash-flow forecast wearing a price tag; reverse-engineering that forecast tells you how much room remains for error.
epigraph.author: Expectations Investing Principle

web_blocks.title: Market Baseline Disclosure & Multi-Year Valuation Multiple Regime

web_blocks.html: All entry zones and return checks in this dossier use the verified NSE close of ₹1,807.20 from November 12, 2026. That close sits 1.11% lower on the day and 2.83% below the ₹1,859.90 52-week high. Morning feeds on November 13 showed TradingView at ₹1,823.00 and StockAnalysis at ₹1,831.70 [26, 27]. That small 1% intraday gap does not change our verified close rules.

At ₹1,807.20 across roughly 57.53 crore shares, equity value stands at ₹1,03,970 Cr [1, 24]. Subtracting September 30 net cash of ₹1,812 Cr (USD 189 million) leaves an Enterprise Value (EV) of ₹1,02,158 Cr [1]. Dividing ₹1,807.20 by Screener's TTM EPS of ₹70.23 yields a trailing P/E of 25.73x [28]. Intraday screens show 25.9x to 26.5x on ₹69.02 StockAnalysis TTM EPS [24, 27]. On consensus numbers, shares trade at 22.35x FY27E EPS (₹80.86) and 18.91x FY28E EPS (₹95.57) [26].

History proves how much re-rating already happened. Over the past five years, Aurobindo traded at a median trailing P/E of 19.9x, spanning 11.8x to 25.6x [28]. StockAnalysis annual ratios likewise show trailing P/E rising from 14.79x in FY22 and 15.75x in FY23 to 21.62x in FY26 and 26.46x today [29]. EV/EBITDA climbed from 7.81x in FY23 and 11.01x in FY26 to 13.49x today [27, 29]. After a 47-week rally (+44.59%), shares stand 29% above their five-year median P/E.

web_blocks.title: Reverse DCF: What Cash-Flow Path Is Priced Into ₹1,02,158 Cr EV

web_blocks.html: Working backward from Enterprise Value exposes the exact cash burden priced into ₹1,807.20. We discount free cash flow at 10.5% WACC with a 4.5% terminal growth rate after Year 10. Two cash baselines frame the hurdle clearly.

First, start straight from FY26 reported Free Cash Flow of ₹2,468 Cr [4, 24]. Justifying ₹1,02,158 Cr EV from that base requires ~15.9% yearly FCF growth for ten years to reach ~₹10,800 Cr in FY36. Second, deduct routine maintenance capex of USD 200 million (~₹1,700 Cr) from ₹5,526 Cr FY26 CFO to get ₹3,826 Cr normalized ex-greenfield FCF [2, 4]. Even from that higher base, current price still assumes 10.1% yearly FCF growth for ten straight years (~₹10,000 Cr in Year 10). Very little room exists for price erosion or plant stalls.

web_blocks.takeaway: At ₹1,807.20, Aurobindo trades near 18.9x FY28E EPS and prices 10.1% normalized FCF growth. It sits 29% above its 5-year median P/E with modest margin of safety [26, 28].

web_blocks.title: Why Aurobindo Costs Half as Much as Domestic Majors—Yet More Than Lupin

web_blocks.html: Peer comps reveal both Aurobindo's discount and its hidden premium. Sun Pharma (37.0x Screener P/E, 20.5% ROCE), Cipla (36.8x, 15.5% ROCE), Dr. Reddy's (41.6x, 13.0% ROCE), and sterile maker Gland Pharma (43.8x, 15.1% ROCE) command 37x–44x earnings. Aurobindo trades 11 to 18 turns cheaper due to 12.9% ROCE, 326 inventory days, and Eugia FDA Warning Letters [8, 9, 24].

Now look at Lupin for contrast. Lupin trades at just 16.4x Screener P/E (17.74x TradingView) despite 29.9% ROCE, 23.75% TV operating margins, and +24.22% sales growth. Why does Aurobindo fetch 9 more P/E turns than Lupin? Price trends answer cleanly. Aurobindo sits in a 47-week Stage 2 uptrend aided by Penicillin-G scale and Lannett. Meanwhile, Lupin remains in Stage 4 Markdown on the daily ledger below its falling 50-DMA (₹2,036.57) and 200-DMA (₹2,237.19), with weekly snapshot screens flagging Stage 1 rebuilding under ₹2,217.23.

web_blocks.takeaway: Aurobindo trades cheaper than Sun, Cipla, Dr. Reddy's, and Gland on lower ROCE (12.9%) and Eugia compliance risk. Yet it holds a 9x P/E premium over Stage 1 Lupin [8, 24].

web_blocks.title: Sell-Side Consensus vs. Independent Earnings Normalization

web_blocks.html: Analyst ratings look bullish on the surface across 27 firms: 12 Strong Buy, 7 Buy, 5 Hold, 1 Sell, and 2 Strong Sell [26]. Street revenue forecasts model ₹40,249 Cr in FY27E (+19.60%) and ₹44,875 Cr in FY28E (+11.49%) [26]. Consensus EPS climbs from ₹80.86 in FY27E (+32.32%) to ₹95.57 in FY28E (+18.19%) [26].

Target prices tell a far more sober story. The average 12-month target sits at ₹1,856 (median ₹1,900; high ₹2,195; low ₹1,270) [26]. An average target just 2.7% above ₹1,807.20 proves Q2 FY27's record print (₹10,263 Cr sales, 21.0% margin) is already baked into models [1, 26]. Beating those numbers requires clean Penicillin-G utilization, CuraTeQ approvals, and Eugia FDA remediation [1, 2, 8].

web_blocks.the_number: ₹95.57 FY28E EPS and ₹2,060.00 Base 12–18 Month Target (+13.99% vs. ₹1,807.20 Close)
web_blocks.how_calculated: We multiply FY28E consensus EPS of ₹95.57 by a 21.55x P/E multiple. That sits 8% above the 5-year median 19.9x P/E to reflect net cash and Pen-G scale, while staying ~16 turns under domestic majors [1, 26, 28].
web_blocks.the_inputs: FY27E revenue ₹40,249 Cr rising to ₹44,875 Cr in FY28E; ~21% EBITDA margin; Pen-G scaling from 10,000 toward 12,000 MTPA; USD 200M base capex; ~57.5 Cr shares post-buyback [1, 2, 26].
web_blocks.the_range: Bear Case ₹1,270.00 (17.3x multiple on ~₹73.50 EPS if Eugia stalls); Base Case ₹2,060.00 (21.55x ₹95.57); Bull Case ₹2,520.00 (25.2x upside ₹100 EPS on early Eugia clearance) [26].
web_blocks.if_off: An Eugia Import Alert, renewed 8%–10% US oral deflation, or weak Pen-G spreads drops FY28E EPS toward ₹72–₹75 and pulls P/E down toward historical lows [8, 29].

book_paragraphs: Once you know how a factory runs, you must test what the stock market already demands at today's quote. All entry limits and stops in this book use the verified NSE close of ₹1,807.20 on November 12, 2026. Intraday prices the next morning touched ₹1,823 on TradingView and ₹1,831.70 on StockAnalysis. That small one percent gap leaves our close-based rules intact.

At ₹1,807.20 across roughly 57.53 crore shares, Aurobindo carries an equity value of ₹1,03,970 crore. Subtract ₹1,812 crore of September 2026 net cash to arrive at ₹1,02,158 crore in Enterprise Value. Divide ₹1,807.20 by trailing twelve-month EPS of ₹70.23, and shares trade at 25.7 times trailing earnings—stepping down to 22.35 times FY27 estimates of ₹80.86 and 18.9 times FY28 estimates of ₹95.57.

Compare that price tag with Aurobindo's own past five years. Its five-year median trailing P/E sits at 19.9 times, ranging between 11.8 times and 25.6 times. Annual ratios likewise rose from 14.8 times in FY22 and 15.8 times in FY23 to 21.6 times in FY26 and 26.5 times today. EV/EBITDA expanded from 7.8 times in FY23 to 13.5 times today. After rising 44.6 percent in a 47-week uptrend, shares sit near the top of their historical band.

Next, let us test what cash flow must happen to earn a solid return from ₹1,02,158 crore Enterprise Value. Using a 10.5 percent cost of capital and 4.5 percent terminal growth, we run a Reverse DCF backward from market value. Starting straight from audited FY26 free cash flow of ₹2,468 crore, today's price requires nearly 16 percent annual cash-flow growth for ten straight years—lifting Year 10 free cash flow near ₹10,800 crore.

Let us also test a friendlier normalized baseline. Routine maintenance capex runs about 200 million dollars, or ₹1,700 crore per year, versus ₹3,058 crore spent during FY26's plant wave. Subtracting ₹1,700 crore from ₹5,526 crore operating cash flow yields ₹3,826 crore of steady-state free cash flow. Even from that stronger base, ₹1,807.20 assumes 10.1 percent annual cash growth for ten years. The market clearly expects clean execution ahead.

Look next at peer Indian drugmakers. Sun Pharma, Cipla, Dr. Reddy's, and Gland Pharma sell for 37 to 44 times trailing earnings. Aurobindo looks cheaper at 25.7 times because it earns lower 12.9 percent ROCE, holds 326 days of inventory, and carries active FDA warnings at Eugia. Meanwhile, Lupin earns 29.9 percent ROCE yet sells at 16.4 to 17.7 times because daily averages still show Stage 4 markdown alongside early Stage 1 base-building. Aurobindo's 9-turn premium over Lupin reflects strong Stage 2 momentum and Kakinada Penicillin-G scale.

Finally, read sell-side analyst models carefully. Among 27 analysts on StockAnalysis, 19 rate the stock Buy or Strong Buy, projecting sales to grow 19.6 percent to ₹40,249 crore in FY27 and ₹44,875 crore in FY28. Yet their average twelve-month target sits at ₹1,856—less than three percent above November 12's close. Good Q2 earnings are largely in the price, making entry discipline essential.

Consider one practical way to frame what a ₹1,856 Street target means alongside our ₹2,060 Base Case. Analysts agree the operational rebound is real, yet they refuse to award an unblemished 35-times pharma multiple while Eugia stays under FDA warning. That skepticism keeps a healthy cap on expectations. Any buyer stepping in above support gets paid only if either profits outrun consensus or sterile plants clear inspection sooner than scheduled.

book_callouts.title: Reading a Reverse DCF Without Spreadsheet Mysticism
book_callouts.quote: Never ask what a stock is worth in isolation; ask what ten-year cash-flow growth today's price already assumes.
book_callouts.text: When normalized free cash flow of ₹3,826 crore already requires 10.1 percent annual growth to justify ₹1,807.20, chasing above support removes your margin of safety.

book_subsections.title: Why Good News Is Already Priced Into Today's Quote
paragraphs: Putting history, reverse cash math, peers, and analyst targets together tells a coherent story. Back in FY23, margins dropped to 15 percent and investors left Aurobindo at 15 times earnings and 7.8 times EBITDA. Since then, record ₹10,263 crore sales, 21 percent operating margins, Kakinada Penicillin-G, and Lannett restored market faith.

However, easy multiple expansion has already occurred. Future gains from ₹1,807.20 rely on delivering ₹95.57 FY28 EPS cleanly and fixing Eugia's sterile plants. With our balanced Base Case target at ₹2,060—just 14 percent above today's close—we must inspect the price chart in Chapter 8 to see if reward-to-risk clears our entry bar.

callouts.quote: When average analyst targets sit within five percent of market price, chart structure decides whether entry math works.
callouts.text: Keep our ₹2,060 Base Case target in mind as we measure Aurobindo's 50-day average, support zone, and stop level next.
